answer.text: Selling losing positions to realise losses (tax-loss harvesting) and use inflows

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax-efficient rebalancing tries to bring the portfolio back to its target weights while minimising the tax bill. Two common tools are (i) realising losing positions so the booked capital losses can offset gains elsewhere, and (ii) using fresh inflows to top up underweight assets so that appreciated holdings need not be sold at all. Combined, these reduce the tax drag of routine rebalancing. The Trap: Selling only winners crystallises gains and worsens the tax position; ignoring tax altogether is not 'tax-efficient' by definition; daily rebalancing maximises trading and tax costs rather than minimising them. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook acknowledges taxes as a rebalancing cost and notes that selling appreciated assets attracts tax liability (around p. 396) and discusses US-context wash-sale/January-effect anomalies on pp. 236-237, but does not present tax-loss harvesting or inflow-based rebalancing as named Indian PMS techniques. The framing above is general industry/regulatory knowledge.
